documentation.short: Determines if the project has generated executable (binary) artifacts in the source repository.

Determines if the default and release branches are protected with GitHub's branch protection settings. Not applicable to repositories with branch-protection: managed in create_repos.yaml: they are protected by the org ruleset ospo-managed.

Determines if the project runs tests before pull requests are merged. Not applicable to repositories with topic docs or template. Inconclusive (-1) is not applicable, unless Code-Review counted changesets: then changes reached the default branch without pull requests, and the result is fail.
Determines if the project has an OpenSSF (formerly CII) Best Practices Badge.
Determines if the project requires human code review before pull requests (aka merge requests) are merged.
Determines if the project has a set of contributors from multiple organizations (e.g., companies).
Determines if the project's GitHub Action workflows avoid dangerous patterns.
Determines if the project uses a dependency update tool.

Determines if the project uses fuzzing. Applies only to repositories with more than 5% code in a non-memory-safe language (C, C++, Objective-C, Objective-C++, Assembly); all others are not applicable.
Determines if the project has defined a license.
Determines if the project is "actively maintained".
Determines if the project is published as a package that others can easily download, install, easily update, and uninstall.
Determines if the project has declared and pinned the dependencies of its build process.
Determines if the project uses static code analysis.
Determines if the project has published a security policy.
Determines if the project cryptographically signs release artifacts.
Determines if the project's workflows follow the principle of least privilege.
Determines if the project has open, known unfixed vulnerabilities.
